text:
anya (PM): quick sync  we need to decide how prompt-sets behave in 'Scan' (dense) vs 'Review' (expanded) modes for the new evals scorecard. Figma: https://figma.redwood/scorecard-density - thoughts? :mag_right:
ryan (Design): two modes makes sense. naming idea: 'Scan / Review' instead of Compact/Detailed so it's action-first. Scan emphasizes fast triage, Review for deep digs
lee (Eng): implementation constraints: Scan must not re-order dom nodes, only collapse non-essential nodes. otherwise our visual regression diffing fails when we compare snapshots across runs
nina (Product): approval UX: in Scan mode we want quick approve/reject inline. in Review, we want the full approval panel with reasoning. can we keep both consistent so audit logs capture which mode approval happened in?
ryan (Design): yes — keep the same approve action but change the affordance: tiny icon-only in Scan, labeled CTA in Review. also plan a subtle badge: 'Scan mode' so reviewers know they're in a compressed view
marta (a11y): accessibility checks: icon-only buttons need accessible names, e.g., `aria-label=\"Approve test\"`. Also color changes in Scan reduce contrast on timestamp and chip labels - fails AA small text. Need stronger color tokens or different weight
lee (Eng): good catch. i'll switch chips to filled variant in Scan to keep contrast. also note: collapsing example exchanges to a single-line summary will change content offset in the diff viewer. i'll add stable identifiers `data-eval-id` and `data-run-id` to rows so our diff matcher uses those instead of DOM index
anya (PM): copy: proposed tooltip for the mode toggle: "Switch to Scan to view more tests at a glance". shorter alt: "Scan shows compact rows for quick triage". Prefer the first?
ryan (Design): prefer "Scan shows compact rows for quick triage" (more explicit about rows) but shorten to <= 60 chars. maybe: "Scan: compact rows for quick triage"
lee (Eng): keyboard flow: toggling from Review -> Scan must preserve focus context. if a user is focused on comment box in Review, after toggling we should move focus to the collapsed comment indicator and announce "comments hidden; press enter to open"
marta (a11y): and ensure `aria-live` region announces mode change: "Switched to Scan mode". also when comments are collapsed, their accessible names should include a count, e.g., "3 comments, collapsed"
nina (Product): question: if someone leaves an inline decision in Scan, do we expand that row automatically or leave it collapsed with an indicator? my vote: expand so the reviewer can confirm text before submitting
ryan (Design): expanding could push the list and change scanning rhythm. alternative: open a side flyout with the comment thread anchored to the row. keeps scanning context but shows details. works for small screens too
lee (Eng): flyout is doable, but mobile can't do side flyouts. fallback: modal on small viewports. we'll add `data-view=\"scan\"` and `data-breakpoint` flags so we can choose behavior client-side
marta (a11y): flyout must trap focus and allow `esc` to return focus to the originating row. on mobile modal is fine but ensure body scroll is disabled and focus is set to first focusable in modal
anya (PM): decision: adopt Scan/Review naming, use icon-only inline approve in Scan, full CTA in Review, use flyout for desktop comments and modal for mobile, add stable data attributes for diffs. Lee to prototype focus + diff-id changes in spike
lee (Eng): will do. i'll also add an opt-in user pref to default the dashboard to Scan for heavy users. will push spike by next Tue with a demo link
devnull-bot: staging build scheduled: 2026-05-02T09:30Z will include Scan/Review toggle spike (frontend-only).
ryan (Design): follow-ups: i'll produce two visual variants for the approve affordance and the collapsed comment indicator (with counts). ping me if you want versions with stronger chip contrast
ina (Product): i'll schedule two 15-min usability sessions next week to watch engineers run both flows. aim: measure time-to-approve and error rate when comments are collapsed
marta (a11y): i'll run quick screen-reader walkthrough on both variants before design final. will report any issues in thread
anya (PM): thanks team. i'll update the spec doc and include the copy we agreed. closing after Lee's spike link lands.
